summary: Werner Sundermann (1935–2012) worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1967–1985), the Academy of Sciences of the GDR (~1970–1991), and the Free University of Berlin (~1993–2000).

Werner Thomas (1923–2008) worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Wolfgang Krause (~1946–1950) and Emil Sieg (~1946–1951) and was on the faculty at Goethe University Frankfurt from ~1964 to 1991.
Wes Borton is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at East Carolina University, studied under Derek F. Maher, and was attested studying at the University of Michigan in 2010.

Whalen Lai (b. 1944) works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned a BA at International Christian University (~1963–1967) and a PhD at Harvard (~1970–1975), later holding posts at UIUC (~1976–1978) and UC Davis (~1978–2009).

Whitelaw Ainslie (1767–1837) was an Indology scholar and surgeon. He served as Assistant Surgeon (1788) and Surgeon (1794–1815) for the East India Company and became a Fellow of the Royal Society of Edinburgh in 1829.

Whitley Stokes (1830–1909) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at St Columba's College and Trinity College Dublin (BA 1846–1851), and was taught by Carl Siegfried and Rudolf Thomas Siegfried (~1858–1863).

Whitney Cox specializes in Indology and religious studies. Educated at the University of Virginia and the University of Chicago (PhD 1998–2006), he held posts at SOAS (~2007–2013) and the University of Chicago (~1999–2006; Professor ~2013).

Widi Widiyanto works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Sekolah Tinggi Agama Buddha Maha Prajna (S.Ag 2001–2005, M.Pd.B 2009–2011) and Universitas Hindu Indonesia (Dr 2022–2025), and was appointed Dosen Tetap at STIAB Jinarakkhita in 2022.

Wijesinghe Sugathadasa Karunaratne (1928–1986) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Educated at the University of Ceylon and SOAS (PhD ~1952–1956), he held posts at the University of Ceylon (1952–1973), University of Peradeniya (1964), and University of Kelaniya (~1957–1986).

Wiktor Jan Porzeziński (1870–1929) worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Moscow State University under Filipp Fedorovich Fortunatov, later teaching there (1903–1921), at the University of Warsaw (~1921–1929), and at the Catholic University of Lublin (1922–1929).

Wilber Theodore Elmore (1871–1935) was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He completed a PhD at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln (~1913–1915) and taught at Palmer Theological Seminary in 1925.

Wilbur Stone Deming (1889–1971) worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Brown University (~1908–1912) and Boston University, joined the American Marathi Mission in 1912, and served as Superintendent of the American Mission High School, Ahmednagar, in 1924.

Wilburn Hansen is a scholar of religious studies and Japanology. He completed a master's program at the University of Colorado Boulder and studied at Stanford University under Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt.

Wilfred Cantwell Smith (1916–2000) was a religious studies scholar educated at Toronto, Cambridge, and Princeton (PhD ~1946–1948). He held posts at Forman Christian College (1940–1946), McGill University (1948–1951), and Harvard University (1964–1973, 1978–1985).

Wilfred Harvey Schoff (1874–1932) specialized in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Harvard and the University of Pennsylvania, worked at the Philadelphia Commercial Museum (1900), and lectured at UW–Madison (1901) and UIUC (1903).

Wilfrid Sellars (1912–1989) was a philosopher educated at Michigan, Buffalo, and Oxford. He taught at the University of Iowa (1938–1946), the University of Minnesota (1947–1958), Yale University (1958–1963), and the University of Pittsburgh (1963–1989).
Wilfried Nölle (1925–1997) was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Tübingen under Helmuth von Glasenapp from ~1946 to 1950.

Wilhelm Alexander Unkrig (1883–1956) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kazan Theological Academy (1908) and served as librarian at Anthropos Institute (1924–1926) and Leiden (1936), before lecturing at Goethe University Frankfurt (1943).

Wilhelm Brandenstein (1898–1967) was a linguist and Indo-Iranian scholar. Educated at Innsbruck and Vienna (PhD ~1923–1925) under teachers including Paul Kretschmer and Nikolai Trubetzkoy, he served as institute head at the University of Graz (1941–1967).

Wilhelm Cartellieri (1860–1908) was an Indology scholar who studied at Leipzig, Vienna (PhD 1878–1884) under Georg Bühler, and Innsbruck (Habilitation 1899). He was appointed ao. Professor at the University of Innsbruck in 1902.
